sections.title: Rubber compound options
sections.chip: 🛑 The most expensive default on the website
sections.live: LIVE → EPDM (SELECTED), NBR, Neoprene, SBR — chosen for you, on a part submerged in the fluid

fields.label: A pre-selected compound on a wetted part
paragraphs: 🛑 The plunger is submerged in the pumped fluid on every stroke, so the compound is not a preference — it is the part. EPDM is correct for water, dosing chemicals and brake fluid, and it swells until the plunger jams in its bore in oil, fuel or grease.

The live page picks EPDM for you without asking what is being pumped, and a buyer who takes the default at face value gets a part that either works for years or seizes in weeks, with nothing on the page to tell them which.

The compound default bug runs the length of this site — silicone on all three gaskets pages, FKM on all six oil seals pages, EPDM on the oil filler cap. This is the page where it costs the most, because the fluid is the whole specification. Rule for the developer: on a wetted part, nothing is pre-selected until the fluid is known.
Margo produces every part in every compound it mixes (client-instructed 2026-09-02). Nothing is removed — all eight are ranked by what is being pumped.

sections.title: From compound to certification
sections.chip: Bonding is a step and the page omits it
sections.live: LIVE H2 → From Compound to Certification · six steps · no mention of the metal side

fields.label: Steps
rows: Material compounding — polymer blending, additive integration and batch QC in our in-house lab. The compound is chosen from the fluid the pump moves, since the plunger is submerged in it on every stroke.
Mould design and manufacture in-house, held as a controlled record. Plunger cavities are cut to the diameter tolerance quoted against your bore.
Metal preparation and bonding agent application, where the plunger is bonded to a stem. Degrease, abrade, prime — the bond is made during cure, not afterwards.
Compression moulding, cure and deflash. The sealing band is the critical surface and is finished accordingly.
Quality inspection — plunger diameter and sealing length against the drawing, hardness to the specified tolerance, and bond integrity checked on bonded parts.

Export packaging — industrial packing with documentation. Plungers are packed so the sealing band is not deformed in transit, since a flat spot on that band is a leak on arrival. ISPM-15 treated pallets where timber packaging is used.
fields.note:
🛑 Step 03 is the addition, and it is a capability rather than a rewording. Rubber-to-metal bonding is confirmed in-house and this page never mentions the metal side of the part at all, even though most plungers have one.
Step 05 names bond integrity separately, because a bonded plunger has two ways to fail and the moulding is only one of them.
Step 06 matters here — the sealing band is a precision surface, and a flat spot pressed into it during shipping arrives as a leak

notes: The process block must render from the part record, so bonded parts show step 03 and all-rubber parts do not.
“Rubber-to-metal bonding” is a searched capability and appears nowhere on this website.

fields.label: Credit, an addition, a caution
paragraphs: ISO 9001:2015 claimed and nothing else — no IATF, no TÜV SÜD, no CE marking. The production table prints “On request” rather than inventing figures, and the video says “Film pending”. Four honest calls in one section, on the last page as on the first.
